## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 None of the surveyed secondary literature passages discuss this text directly; occurrences of the name in the literature instead refer either to the *Mahākassapatthera-bojjhaṅga* of the Saṃyutta Nikāya utilized in protective (*paritta*) healing traditions or to the twelfth-century South Indian commentator Mahākassapa.

Textual reuse data computed by DharmaNexus shows extensive sharing between this text and the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, most notably its second volume (Atk S0508a2), which contains ten shared passages spanning more than 4,400 characters, including a long continuous segment matching verses §0.3–23.1 [DharmaNexus]. Additional segments are shared with the first volume of the commentary (Atk S0508a1) [DharmaNexus]. The text also exhibits formulaic reuse shared with other Therāpadāna poems, including the *Mahāmoggallānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 4), *Sopākattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 21), *Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 20), *Piṇḍolabhāradvājattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 10), and *Paṇṇadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 283) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language matches identified by DharmaNexus include an alignment with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (§22.1–22.4 ↔ §328–330; plausibility score 75) and lower-scoring parallels in Tibetan canonical literature, including the *Vinayavastu* (D0001-2) and the *Dīpaṃkaravyākaraṇa* (D0188) [DharmaNexus].
